description: A brick of army compressed ration biscuit in a plain foil wrapper, the kind every Vietnamese soldier, student on a field trip and flood-relief volunteer has chewed through: dense, faintly sweet, and dry enough to need half a bottle of water.  It keeps for years.

A thick Vietnamese Catholic Bible with a cracked black cover, the parish's translation, its thin pages marked with ribbons and a palm leaf from last year's Palm Sunday.  Somebody wrote the family's baptism dates on the flyleaf.

A small, much-thumbed Vietnamese prayer book: morning and evening prayers, the rosary, the Stations of the Cross, hymns for Christmas and Easter.  Old women at the 5 a.m. Mass know every page by heart.

A fat, dog-eared travel guide to Vietnam, 2008 edition, its spine broken at the Saigon chapter: cheap rooms on Phạm Ngũ Lão, how to cross the road (slowly, never stop), bus times to Mũi Né and the Mekong Delta, and a phrasebook in the back.  Someone has underlined "bao nhiêu tiền?" twice.
A high-school literature textbook from the Ministry of Education: poems, essays and model speeches, the exercises on how to argue a point already filled in by its previous owner in purple ink.
A Vietnamese Red Cross first-aid handbook for schools and wards, with line drawings of bandaging, the recovery position, treating burns from the kitchen stove and motorbike-crash injuries.
